fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. David really does list it: "…the one anointed by the God of Jacob…" (2 Samuel 23:1). It's right there in the middle of his titles. The One who anointed him is the God of Jacob.

That's the one. David says, "The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue." (2 Samuel 23:2). The Spirit speaks through David, and the word on his tongue is God's. A good messenger knows whose word he's carrying, and David puts it right up front.

That's right. God's picture has "…the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth." (2 Samuel 23:4). So the grass is glistening after the rain and it's sprouting. No dry, crunchy grass in this one.

That's it. David asks, "Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?" (2 Samuel 23:5). He asks it right after talking about the covenant, so I bet he's leaning on God's promise. He sure sounds confident to me.

A quiet old age sounds lovely, baker. But David doesn't say that here. He asks, "Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?" (2 Samuel 23:5). He's looking for something bigger than a comfy rocking chair.

David defeated the Philistines (2 Samuel 8:1), so I get why you went there. But victory over neighbors isn't what he mentions here. He asks, "Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?" (2 Samuel 23:5). It's about salvation and what he truly desires.
Yes, baker. David says, "But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside…" (2 Samuel 23:6). He adds that "…they can never be gathered by hand." It's a sharp picture, and I think it's meant to be.

Sand on the seashore is a different picture than David's, friend. He says, "…the worthless are all like thorns raked aside…" (2 Samuel 23:6). Then he adds that "…they can never be gathered by hand." Sand doesn't fit that line, since you can scoop it up by the handful.
Cloth feels like a reasonable guess, friend. But David says the man "…must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear." (2 Samuel 23:7). So the word is iron. Cloth isn't on his list.
Reeds are a fair guess, baker. But David says the man "…must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear." (2 Samuel 23:7). So the word is iron. The shaft of a spear is the other choice he gives.

Not quite, baker. David says, "The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie." (2 Samuel 23:7). That's where the verse has them burning, in the place where they lie. The verse doesn't mention any trip.

Correct. David says, "The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie." (2 Samuel 23:7). The verse doesn't mention any trip, just the fire and the place where they lie. And that's how the poem ends.
